title: Refuelling-Area Safety Pattern
body: ADW has had four refuelling-point incidents in thirteen months: the MG-85 wall strike, a diesel overflow, a contractor fuel truck unloading with its driver asleep, and NCR 25-037. Every one was a supervision gap, not a fire-control gap. On the production side, go-line queues and a dry tank are now one of the three biggest drivers of truck idle hours.
keyPoints: SOP 20 covers fire hazards (engine off, no phones, extinguisher, spill trays). It does not require a spotter. Any large HME backing into a tight bay needs a named assistant guiding it. MG-85 hit the wall because nobody was there.
No machine moves while the fuel truck or tanker is manoeuvring nearby. Both the gas-station and MG-85 events had a vehicle moving near an active delivery.
Check the handle and nozzle before every fill. A stone on the fuel handle caused the 24-Jun overflow, and the check takes seconds.
Check the spill kit and fire extinguisher at every fuelling point. Don't assume they're there. At the gas-station event, neither was on hand.
Fuel at shift change and start-up, not mid-shift. The go-line holds only 35,000 L, so one late delivery empties it. That happened on 8-Sep.
apply: At start-up, watch the North Go Line. Check whether an attendant is at the bay and whether the second dispensing point is actually in use. If trucks are queuing past 07:30, fix it on the spot rather than logging it as another lost hour.
